plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs to zero.

conservative.read: This plan focuses on capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% per month. It significantly reduces risk by cutting leveraged positions and weak names, aiming for low drawdowns. Expect slower growth due to reduced leverage and concentration.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs to small positions.
Reduce exposure to weaker AI/Software names.
Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration.
This plan balances risk reduction with growth potential.
It aims for steady, risk-first growth.
A moderate cash buffer will be held.
balanced.read: This balanced approach targets around 2.5% per month by reducing leverage and concentration while maintaining some growth exposure. It aims for a risk-first growth profile with moderate drawdowns. Expect growth to be steadier than aggressive but higher than conservative.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to manage concentration.

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets around 4% per month by leaning into leverage and strong scanner setups, accepting higher risk. Expect amplified gains but also significantly larger potential drawdowns and the impact of leveraged ETF decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and weak AI/Software names.

This plan prioritizes steady monthly distributions.
It aims for low drawdowns and reliable income.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% per month by rotating into income-generating assets like QQQI. It prioritizes low drawdowns and consistent monthly distributions over growth. While NAV can still fall, the focus is on generating yield, not capital appreciation.
